newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish C/A deficit seen at $6-7 bln at end-1996.
newsitem.headline: Turkish C/A deficit seen at $6-7 bln at end-1996.

text.p: Turkish central bank governor Gazi Ercel said Turkey's current account deficit was forecast to rise to $6-$7 billion at end-1996, up sharply from $2.3 billion last year.
He said the public sector borrowing requirement (PSBR) was expected to reach nine to 10 percent of gross national product after 6.5 percent in 1995.
"The current account deficit is estimated to rise to $6-$7 billion this year. But it is easily being financed by unregistered exports of some $5 to $10 billion," Ercel told Reuters.
He was referring to the so-called luggage trade mostly by East Europeans, Russians and Central Asians who come to Turkey as tourists but buy mainly Turkish textile products.
Ercel said the 1996 budget's primary surplus -- the budget balance excluding debt interest payments -- was likely to reach one to two percent of the GNP.
